articles.title: VisionQuest Post-Credits Scene Just Confirmed A Major Marvel Character Is Coming Back in Upcoming Avengers Films
articles.summary: Spoilers for VisionQuest and potentially Avengers: Doomsday are contained in the article below. You've been warned! The finale of VisionQuest confirmed that one of the most beloved characters from the MCU will be returning in the upcoming Avengers films, seemingly under the control of Doctor Doom.
body: Following the conclusion of VisionQuest, Marvel snuck in a little teaser for Avengers: Doomsday and/or Secret Wars during the credits. The scene was excluded from advanced screeners provided to the press, so it came as a big surprise and shows that Marvel made a great deal of effort to keep this moment a secret.

The show cut back to the ending of Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness, where Wanda Maximoff, AKA Scarlet Witch, uses her powers to destroy the Darkhold and, in the process, sacrifices herself. Her fate has remained unknown for over four years now, but now, we finally know what's next for her.

Doctor Doom shows up and lifts a bunch of rubble off of her, uttering the words: "Scarlet Witch, awaken. Your power will be mine." Her eyes open in shock before the scene cuts to black. The plot of Avengers: Doomsday has remained relatively abstract for some time now. Universes are starting to catastrophically collide as part of a series of "incursions," but the why and how of it all has remained a secret. Doom's larger plan and motive have also been kept under wraps, but we've started to get a better idea over the last couple of months.

The finale of VisionQuest confirmed that one of the most beloved characters from the MCU will be returning in the upcoming Avengers films, seemingly under the control of Doctor Doom.

articles.title: Marvel's VisionQuest Series Finale Review: 'Forever'
articles.summary: The last-minute addition of a new villain derails the finale of VisionQuest somewhat, but the series still succeeds where Vision and Ultron are concerned.
body: VisionQuest has certainly gained momentum with time, to the point where it easily ranks among the best of Marvel's live-action Disney+ shows to date (not that it looks like there's going to be much competition in the foreseeable future ). Sadly, that momentum doesn't entirely carry over into the final episode. "Forever" is a bit of a letdown compared to recent installments of the series, mainly due to the last-minute pivot to a new villain.

Part of it comes down to the notion that Ultron is based on a human model in the first place. The series lightly teased this a few episodes back when Ultron insisted to F.R.I.D.A.Y. that he was unique. Well, it turns out he isn't. It diminishes this villain a bit to see that all his acerbic, affected charm comes not from being invented in a lab by Tony Stark and immediately exposed to the horrors of the Internet, but because he's a copy of Jo Carrington's (T'Nia Miller) creepy ex-boyfriend. Ultimately, I might have been happier if the series had culminated with the more predictable reveal that Phineas Horton (Paul Bettany) or J.I.M. were the Client.

articles.title: Fortis Games Closes With Over 400 Jobs Impacted
articles.summary: Fortis Games, a studio behind mobile titles like Twilight Towers and Bloom & Breakfast, has closed its doors, impacting around 440 jobs. CEO Steven Chiang confirmed the closure in a statement to GamesBeat on November 10, 2026.
body: “We have been fortunate to work with some of the most talented and dedicated people in this space. As we move forward, our primary focus will be on helping this talented team of individuals find new opportunities. Thank you to everyone who has supported us over the past five years. We are grateful for the collaboration and friendship we have shared with so many.”

Several former employees have spoken out about the closure in posts on LinkedIn. In one of these posts, game producer Gustavo Coronet confirmed that Las Vegas Sands Corp., Fortis Games’ parent company, chose to “end funding and part ways, terminating all of the contracts, worldwide.”

“Super proud of the work we’ve done. LVS’s decision does not delete the ground breaking and best-in class agentic development workflow the Octopus team has built, nor the massively solid soft launch metrics both our projects were achieving in such early stages of development,” he wrote.

In another post, former communications director Scott Butterworth suggested that Fortis’s “community-focused” approach to mobile games didn’t resonate enough with players to help it “get off the ground.”

articles.title: The DCU Regime Change Threatens to Turn Man of Tomorrow Into 2027’s Answer to The Flash
articles.summary: It’s fall 2022 and a new regime is announced as taking over DC’s film and TV future even as a major DC movie from the prior regime continues in post-production for release the following summer.
body: It’s been four years since James Gunn and Peter Safran were announced as the co-bosses of DC Studios, and just a day since their ouster was revealed, and this nerd reporter is having a serious case of déjà vu.
When Gunn and Safran took the reins of DC in October 2022, they were inheriting several projects that were already far into production: the headline-plagued The Flash, Blue Beetle, and Batgirl.

In 2023, The Flash marked the end of a DC film continuity created just a handful of years earlier — the DCEU, aka the Snyderverse — that would see a group of DC heroes, including Supergirl, band together to stop a cosmic threat to Earth led by one of Superman’s greatest foes.

In 2027, Man of Tomorrow will potentially mark the end of a DC film continuity created just a handful of years earlier — the DCU — that will see a group of DC heroes, including Supergirl, band together to stop a cosmic threat to Earth led by one of Superman’s greatest foes.

articles.title: Sony Cancels Live-Service PS5 Game Fairgames, But No Layoffs
articles.summary: Sony has canceled the upcoming live-service shooter Fairgame$, but there will be no job cuts connected to the game's closure. This is according to a report from Bloomberg today. The game was in the works at Haven Studios in Montreal, a team founded by former Assassin's Creed veteran Jade Raymond.
body: According to the report, Haven "reworked" the Fairgame$ concept several times in the past three years. The studio was reportedly planning to re-reveal it with a new name. Going forward, Haven staff will support other PlayStation projects, the report said.
Fairgame$ was officially canceled following a playtest that didn't show strong results.

“While the test demonstrated strong operational excellence, live ops readiness and community engagement, player feedback and retention results were mixed and fell short of the goals we had set,” PlayStation executives Sean Decker and John Doyle said in a memo seen by Bloomberg. "Combined with challenging market conditions in the PVP shooter genre, we have made the difficult decision to cease development on the game.”

Creative director Mathieu Leduc said in a blog post that Haven was founded with the goal of making games that its staffers wanted to play, and that’s why the team chose a competitive multiplayer game.
points: Sony has canceled the upcoming live-service shooter Fairgame$, but there will be no job cuts connected to the game's closure.

articles.title: GTA 6 Backflips Look Good Now, But There Could Be More To The Story
articles.summary: A new Grand Theft Auto 6 trailer debuted today, November 10, and the video showed off a race car driver doing a backflip. The animation looks smoooth. That's notable because the Extended Look trailer that debuted back in August showed Jason doing a backflip and people online quickly roasted it for…
body: That's because it subsequently came to light that the backflip animation in GTA 6 is controlled by the player and isn't locked to one specific animation. However, we don't know who is doing the backflip in this newest clip.
If the character in the trailer is an NPC, as people on Reddit are surmising, then the animation could have been motion-captured as opposed to being player-controlled, hence why it looks less janky.

In any event, this backflip stuff becoming a "controversy," if you can even call it that, is yet another example of how ramped-up people are for GTA 6. People are so jazzed for the release that they are poring over even the smallest details, which you may never even notice when playing the game for yourself.

GTA 6 releases on November 19 for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S, and preloading is live now. The game unlocks at midnight local time on November 19, and that means people in the US will be among the last in the world to play.

articles.title: Amid Higher Gas And Grocery Prices, GTA 6 Is A “Bargain” At $80, Take-Two CEO Says
articles.summary: It's no secret that life is expensive. Gas and grocery prices are up, in particular, and against that backdrop, Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick believes GTA 6 at $80 is a "bargain" due to how many hours people can play it. "I think the consumer is under pressure. these are challenging times.
body: What gives Zelnick hope in this environment is that, in his belief, "interactive entertainment is actually a real bargain," and particularly a game like GTA.

"There are so many hours of engagement on offer. Even a short video game is 10 hours of engagement on the low end. You can play Grand Theft Auto 5 for hundreds of hours and not get bored. We'll see how people feel about Grand Theft Auto 6, but I believe that you'll be able to engage for an extraordinary long period of time," he said. "So if consumers look at entertainment value as the intersection of how great it is and how long you can engage with it, interactive entertainment is a great bargain. However, when you give people what they want, no matter what the times are, they will show up for it."
points: Gas and grocery prices are up, in particular, and against that backdrop, Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick believes GTA 6 at $80 is a "bargain" due to how many hours people can play it.

articles.title: Steam's age verification in Australia now takes your account's age into consideration
articles.summary: Jody's first computer was a Commodore 64, so he remembers having to use a code wheel to play Pool of Radiance. A former music journalist who interviewed everyone from Giorgio Moroder to Trent Reznor, Jody also co-hosted Australia's first radio show about videogames,
body: In compliance with local laws, Steam rolled out age verification in Australia two months ago. Controversially, it was based on whether you owned a credit card, which many Australians do not. Overnight, Australians stopped being able to see games that are rated R18+ in the Steam store, like Doom, if they didn't have a credit card linked to their account.

Just as suddenly, Steam support has now updated how age verification works for Australians. Adding a credit card to your account still works, but additionally: "Steam will automatically consider your account age verified if it is at least nine years old and has had a consistent email address or billing information."

If you've moved house in the last nine years and let Steam know about it then your billing information won't have been consistent, so I sure hope you haven't changed both your email and physical address in that time.

articles.summary: The fire’s burning low. The road ahead looks grim. The companion who has spent half your journey needling you clearly has something on their mind, and you’re one or two correct dialogue choices away from getting them to spill. You pick a reply. You feel it land.
body: It may be unlikely that we’ll see a new Dragon Age title anytime soon. (Earlier this month, former Dragon Age writer David Gaider said that “the golden days are over.”) Yet there are still campfires worth stopping at. If you miss that feeling of saving Thedas by day and hanging out with your party of oddball companions by night, check out these four upcoming RPGs. Consider this your recruitment screen.

You can never keep every companion happy in Dragon Age. Solasta 2 eases you into this never-ending quest for balance by starting you off with your family. You lead the Colwall siblings, orphans from a household tied to a religious order sworn against an evil called Shadwyn. Soon, the siblings travel to a new continent, where the opening city, Caer Mar, comes with rebels, factions, and plenty of trouble.

articles.title: One Elder Scrolls fan is reviving and upgrading (with AI) a lost spin-off for the Nokia N-Gage and porting it to PC
articles.summary: I spend way too much time on wikis reading about spin-off games made for handheld and mobile devices I will probably never play (there was a whole trilogy of Silent Hill: Orphan games that have lived up to their name by being orphaned on old phones).
body: This first-person RPG is about to return thanks to Dan Whelan, whose Shadowkey Reforged project will let us play Shadowkey in widescreen with controller support and upscaled graphics. You can choose to play in classic or modern mode, but you can also toggle individual features one by one. Modern mode isn't just a graphical upgrade as it also adds features from the later mainline Elder Scrolls games like stamina-based sprinting, stealth, and ragdoll physics.

This is one of those times where I prefer the original game's look, as the brutally abrupt draw distance leaves a lot to your imagination while the modernized version seems to show enemies looming unresponsively in the near distance. And it's not like the upscaled character models actually look good, despite being beyond what Nokia's taco phone was capable of displaying.

While Shadowkey was never particularly well-ranked in the pantheon of Elder Scrolls games, people did praise its use of the Morrowind soundtrack, which Shadowkey Reforged will continue. Point it to your Morrowind install and it'll borrow both music and sound effects from the best Elder Scrolls game.

articles.title: Sony cancels another live service game ahead of release, but at least there won't be any layoffs this time
articles.summary: A Bloomberg report says Fairgames, a PvP heist shooter announced by Haven Studios and Sony in 2023, has been cancelled. In something of a surprising twist, a PlayStation rep told the site there will be no layoffs as a result of the cancellation, as Haven will "shift its focus to collaborating with…
body: While it was announced three years ago, work on Fairgames appears to have started even further back, in 2021. Just a couple months after her high-profile split with Google Stadia, Assassin's Creed co-creator Jade Raymond announced the formation of Haven Studios, which was "working on an unannounced new IP for PlayStation."

In 2022, right around the time former PlayStation boss Jim Ryan was talking about launching 12 live service games by 2025, Sony acquired the studio outright; a year after that, Fairplay was revealed to the world.

But things have not gone smoothly since then. Helldivers 2 was a massive hit, but seven of those planned games were cancelled before release. Of the remaining games, one was Marathon, which endures but has not lived up to expectations, and another was Concord, one of the most famously disastrous game launches in years, which was taken offline less than two weeks after it launched, never to return. A live-service spinoff of the Horizon series, Hunters Gathering, was also reportedly rebooted after negative feedback from playtests.
